newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors to appeal Chun, Roh sentences.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors to appeal Chun, Roh sentences.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors will appeal to the Supreme Court over sentences handed out to former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, a senior prosecutor said on Monday.
An appeals court last Monday commuted Chun's death sentence to life in jail and slashed Roh's prison term to 17 years from 22-1/2 years. Prosecutors are seeking heavier punishment.

Prosecutor Kim Sang-hee said prosecutors would also challenge court decisions on 13 others who stood trial with Chun and Roh on mutiny, treason and bribery charges, including former aides, one-time generals and businessmen.
Two of the businessmen -- Hanbo Group honorary chairman Chung Tai-soo and Lee Kyung-hoon, former president of Daewoo Corp -- were acquitted by the appeals court.
Earlier, lawyers for Chun and Roh said their clients would not challenge the appeal's court verdicts.
Separately, appeals were lodged by 13 former generals, three former presidential aides and two businessmen, including the chairman of Daewoo and Dong Ah groups, a court official said.
